title: Stabilize scheduler ↔ attention kernel coordination after surge-induced misrouting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a high-concurrency capacity surge on 2026-02-26 we observed sustained p95/p99 latency regressions for a subset of customer traffic. Root cause analysis shows the scheduler started routing requests with mid-length sequences to an attention-optimized kernel variant that had been recently enabled behind a probe flag. That kernel interacts poorly with the mixed-quantization path (int4 mixed with float16) for certain layers, leading to intermittent KV-cache misses and execution stalls. The misrouting amplified under burst conditions due to probe amplification and lack of hysteresis, causing path-flapping and a localized reduction in throughput.

This ticket captures remediation actions, short-term mitigations, and the medium-term engineering work to prevent recurrence and improve observability of path selection correctness.
timeline:
2026-02-26 03:14 UTC: first alerts (increased p95)
2026-02-26 03:22 UTC: Ops rerouted a subset of traffic to stable model variant (manual rollback)
2026-02-26 06:00 UTC: Investigations team reproduced increased KV miss rate on synthetic replay
2026-02-27 10:30 UTC: Kernel dev identified an incompatibility between the new attn-optimized path and mixed-quantized Conv1 layer in model family X
2026-02-28 09:00 UTC: Decision to pause probe rollout and add scheduler hysteresis
2026-03-02 to 2026-03-08: Benchmarks and mutating fixes validated on canary pools
2026-03-10: Initial mitigation deployed to production (probe gating + probe saturation limiter)
root_cause: Two combined regressions: (1) a newly enabled attention-optimized kernel variant had edge-case numeric/ordering behavior with our mixed-quantization execution path, causing transient KV-cache misses and execution slowdowns; (2) the scheduler's probe amplification logic lacked sufficient damping and hysteresis under bursty arrivals, resulting in coordinated misrouting (path-flapping) that amplified the impact across workers.
impact: Customer-facing: increased generation latency (p95 up to 3x for affected routes) and occasional token gaps for 12% of requests to the X-model family during the surge window. Internally: autoscaling reacted slower than expected, driving a temporary capacity shortage and elevated infra costs for the mitigation period.
short_term_mitigations: - Gate the attention-optimized probe flag off (done 2026-02-28) - Add probe-saturation limiter to scheduler (deployed 2026-03-10) - Automatic rollback policy for model-path latency regressions (PR #3521) - Temporary routing rule: pin traffic from high-QPS customers on X-model family to legacy kernel variant until canary validated
medium_term_actions: - Kernel team: patch mixed-quant execution ordering in attn-optimized variant and add deterministic numeric regression tests (owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 2026-03-18) - Scheduler: implement hysteresis and exponential backoff for probe-driven switches, add per-route probe budget accounting (owner: Daniel Kim, ETA: 2026-03-20) - Batching/Cache: instrument per-request KV-cache provenance and add alerts for sudden per-worker cache miss spikes (owner: Miguel Alvarez, ETA: 2026-03-22) - Release: include a 'compatibility matrix' in the model onboarding checklist that validates kernel/quantization combos (owner: Runtime QA, ETA: 2026-03-25)
owners: Asha Patel - incident commander / PM follow-up
acceptance_criteria:
- No reproduction of path-flapping under synthetic burst tests for 72h on staging
- p95 latency regression absent in canary for 7 continuous days after deployment of kernel fix and scheduler hysteresis
- New alerts trigger on >15% per-worker KV-cache miss delta within 5 minutes (tested and operational)
- Post-deployment runbook updated and runbook drill completed with on-call within 2 weeks
updates: 2026-03-01: Kernel team reproduced numeric divergence on instrumented microbench (Priya) - fix prototype in review
2026-03-05: Scheduler hysteresis RFC reviewed by infra and runtime; agreed on probe-budget design (design doc: /docs/scheduler-hysteresis.md)
2026-03-10: Probe-saturation limiter deployed to production (canary -> 100%) with no regression observed in next 24h
2026-03-12: QA validated kernel patch on mixed-quant model set; prepping release cut for runtime-1.24.1
notes:
Design trade-offs: stronger hysteresis increases convergence time after real beneficial probe discoveries — we bound this with a per-route probe budget so high-variance routes still explore but cannot amplify across workers. We rejected per-request sticky routing due to memory overhead and complexity for autoscaling.

Follow-ups: schedule a cross-team post-deploy review 2 weeks after runtime-1.24.1 rollout to validate KPIs and update the model onboarding checklist. Also consider adding a lightweight 'canary certificate' that a kernel variant must pass before being probed at scale.
